label: rem:level-zero-discards-braid-noncommutativity
title: Level-0 discards braid non-commutativity at every $n \geq 3$, not only the non-extremal blocks at $n \geq 4$
html:
The statement records that for n \geq 4 the Hecke algebra carries irreducible representations beyond the three extremal ones, and that the invariants they produce are not captured by the 2 \times 2 transfer matrix. That is a statement about the count of blocks. It is not a statement that the transfer-matrix construction is complete below n = 4, and reading it as one overstates the theorem.

A second approximation is present at every n \geq 3, independent of the block count. Step 2 of the proof forms the chained element X_i = \prod_{j > i} X_j inside the two-dimensional crossing algebra R[\sigma] = R[x] / \bigl((x - q)(x + q^{-1})\bigr), which is commutative, and sets M_i = T(X_i). The crossings so chained belong to different strand pairs, and the corresponding braid generators do not commute in H_n(q) for any n \geq 3. The Level-0 reduction therefore discards braid non-commutativity as well as the non-extremal blocks, and only the second of those is an n \geq 4 effect.

The two are easy to conflate because the dimensions agree at n = 3: the standard block of H_3(q) has dimension n - 1 = 2, and so does R[\sigma]. This is a coincidence of dimension, not an identification. By Step 2 the two eigenvalues of M_i are the symmetric and alternating characters \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} and \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}, so the standard representation does not act on M_i at all; the row labelled standard in the correspondence table records the Markov functional \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i) = z \, (M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22} on the crossing algebra, not an image of the two-dimensional block.

Deuterium is the unique atom with n = A + Z = 3. It is therefore both the smallest atom carrying two distinct braid generators and the only one at which the extremal blocks exhaust the partitions, which makes it the single point at which the two approximations can be separated. Evaluating the functional there gives

  \alpha\bigl(
    \Phi_1 - 2[3]_q \cdot \Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \cdot \Phi_3
  \bigr)
  \approx -6.214 \; \mathrm{MeV},

against a measured -B(\mathrm{D}) \approx -2.225 \; \mathrm{MeV}. Since no non-extremal block exists at n = 3, the discrepancy is attributable to the Level-0 reduction alone. It bounds the magnitude of that one approximation and excludes no ingredient of the construction. The evaluation, together with checks of the Step 2 readouts and of the commutativity of R[\sigma] against the non-commutativity of H_3(q), is carried out in computations/probes/level0_reduction_is_not_an_exactness_claim_probe.py.
